title: Them, -ir & -re verbs, can I?
summary: les = them (people or things). It sounds like 'lay', which is different from le. Before a vowel the s links as a z: les inviter. Verbs can end in -er, -ir (finir) or -re (attendre = to wait for). 'Can I…?' as an inversion is the special form Puis-je… ?
points: les = them, for both masculine and feminine. Say 'lay', not 'luh', or it sounds like le.
Liaison: les inviter, les attendre. The s sounds like z.
Liaison happens mostly between words tightly linked in meaning.
attendre = to wait for. No 'for' needed: Je veux l'attendre.
Puis-je… ? = Can I…? An old form that survives only in this question.
